blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Looking across the period, Detached houses: 11 sold over 4 months against an average of 16.0 listed, about 5.8 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was June with 3 sold. Condos and townhomes: 8 sold over 4 months against an average of 9.5 listed, about 4.8 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was June with 2 sold.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Glenbrooke North

items.t: Glenbrooke North is a mainland residential neighbourhood north of Queen's Park, around Glenbrook Ravine, Jamieson Court and Park Crescent. The City spells the name "Glenbrooke North" and lists it among its Historic Neighbourhood Context Statements; SnapStats spells it "GlenBrooke North." Precise OCP boundary roads: UNVERIFIED — no City page read states a surveyed boundary.

Nearby areas: Queens Park (the Heritage Conservation Area) to the south, Sapperton to the east across McBride Boulevard, Massey Victory Heights beyond Sapperton, and Downtown / Uptown to the south-west. Identity note: Glenbrooke North is a real City-recognised neighbourhood name, but it is NOT a Heritage Conservation Area — the Queen's Park HCA adjoins it to the south and its permit rules do not extend into Glenbrooke North on any source read.

Parks and recreation: Glenbrook Ravine park and trail run through the area, and Queen's Park (arena, sportsplex, stadium, sports fields) sits at the south edge. The city's main aquatic centre, the təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre, 65 East Sixth Avenue, is in Uptown. Library: Main Branch, New Westminster Public Library, 716 6th Avenue. Health care: Royal Columbian Hospital, 330 East Columbia Street, in Sapperton, and Queens Park Care Centre, 315 McBride Blvd, at the Queen's Park edge. Shopping: no shopping centre inside Glenbrooke North was confirmed on an official source: UNVERIFIED.

Roads and transit: 8th Avenue, 8th Street and McBride Boulevard serve the area, linking south to Downtown and the Pattullo Bridge approach and north to East Columbia Street in Sapperton. No SkyTrain station is inside Glenbrooke North; the nearest are Columbia Station and Sapperton Station (Expo Line); TransLink routes 123 (New Westminster Station / Brentwood Station) and 102 (Victoria Hill / New Westminster Station) serve the north mainland corridors. Commute times in minutes: UNVERIFIED.

Schools: SD40 catchments are address-based. For the sample address 91 Courtney Crescent, the SD40 School Locator result recorded in the master research (locator run 2026-10-21) is F.W. Howay Elementary (K–5), École Glenbrook Middle (6–8) and New Westminster Secondary (9–12) — a completed locator run for that sample address ONLY; the locator also shows Early French Immersion at École Herbert Spencer Elementary and Montessori (K–5) at Skwo:wech Elementary for this address (Programs of Choice, not catchment schools).

Market context, labelled correctly: September 2026 SnapStats — Glenbrooke North sub-area detached inventory 17 / solds 2 (12% ratio) and "Condos & Townhomes" combined inventory 10 / solds 2 (20% ratio), a small sample in both segments; New Westminster community detached median $1,365,000 and condos & townhomes median $560,000. Sub-area medians: UNVERIFIED (community level only).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Glenbrooke North

items.t: Zoning — Zoning Bylaw No. 6680, 2001: houses sit under the RS series (s.310) — RS-1 minimum site 557.40 sq. m. (6,000 sq. ft.), FSR 0.5; RM-1 (s.420) caps site coverage at 40% and density at 35 units per net acre / FSR 1.2 where designated.

Ravine / streamside diligence: Glenbrook Ravine is a watercourse corridor in the City Green Zone; streamside setback detail for a specific lot: UNVERIFIED — check ravine setbacks before promising additions on ravine-edge lots. Parks and Open Space.pdf

Heritage context (not a permit layer here): the Glenbrooke North / Queen's Park context work documents some of the city's oldest dwellings in this combined area — context documentation is not HCA protection, and no HCA covers Glenbrooke North on the sources read.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Glenbrooke North ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR.

blocks.text: Good to know about Glenbrooke North

items.t: Old houses, no heritage permit layer: the combined Glenbrooke North / Queen's Park context work documents some of the city's oldest dwellings here, yet no HCA covers Glenbrooke North — a buyer gets the Queen's Park–area streetscape and an in-area middle school without the HCA permit layer, on the sources read.

The ravine quietly shrinks lots: Glenbrook Ravine–edge lots can carry streamside setbacks that reduce buildable area below what the RS-1 site area suggests — the setback, not the zone minimum, is the binding number on those parcels, and it is lot-specific. Parks and Open Space.pdf

faq.q: Is Glenbrooke North inside the Queen's Park Heritage Conservation Area?
faq.a: No — the HCA covers the Queen's Park neighbourhood to the south; Glenbrooke North adjoins it, is documented in the City's Historic Neighbourhood Context Statements, and carries no HCA permit layer on the sources read. Confirm any specific address with the City.

faq.q: What sold in Glenbrooke North in September 2026?
faq.a: Detached: 2 solds from 17 listings (12% sales ratio); condos & townhomes: 2 solds from 10 listings (20%) — a small sample in both segments. At the New Westminster community level the detached median sale price was $1,365,000 and the condos & townhomes median was $560,000 (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats GVR September 2026 report).

School District 40, address-based. For the sample address 91 Courtney Crescent the locator result is F.W. Howay Elementary (K–5), École Glenbrook Middle (6–8) and New Westminster Secondary (9–12); Glenbrook Middle School, 701 Park Crescent, is in the area.
None is in the sub-area; the nearest are Columbia Station and Sapperton Station on the Expo Line, with TransLink routes 123 and 102 serving the north mainland corridors.

faq.q: Can I buy a vacant lot in Glenbrooke North?
faq.a: No verified one — no named bare-land subdivision, bare-land strata or presale lot offering was verified; the stock is established RS house lots and built strata.

faq.q: How small can a lot be, and can I split one?
faq.a: RS-1 sets a minimum site of 557.40 sq. m. (6,000 sq. ft.) with FSR 0.5; RM-1, where designated, caps coverage at 40% and density at FSR 1.2. Subdivision runs under Bylaw No. 7142, 2007, with Approving Officer approval and adequate servicing.

faq.q: What do RT-A and RT-B allow here?
faq.a: Nothing — those districts do not exist in New Westminster.

faq.q: What does a ravine-edge lot need checked?
faq.a: Streamside setbacks — Glenbrook Ravine is a watercourse corridor in the City Green Zone and setbacks are lot-specific (UNVERIFIED per lot). Check them before promising additions. Parks and Open Space.pdf
